questions.prompt: Explain how a nephron produces urine.
questions.modelAnswer: Blood enters the glomerulus at high pressure, and small molecules (water, glucose, salts, urea) are filtered into Bowman’s capsule. As the filtrate passes along the tubule, useful substances like glucose, amino acids, salts and most of the water are selectively reabsorbed into the surrounding blood capillaries. The remaining fluid, water with urea and excess salts, is urine, which goes to the collecting duct.
